Even the most carefully designed fiber optics system may develop a problem at some time.
INTRODUCTIONM
Combining an understanding of the system's operation with a well developed troubleshooting strategy is necessary for finding and correcting the problem.
Let's begin the lesson on FIBER OPTIC SYSTEM TROUBLESHOOTING...............
LESSON MENU
TROUBLESHOOTING STRATEGY
A properly operating fiber optic system will have an output signal that is equivalent to the input signal.
DISCUSSION

Be aware that some variations between the input and output signals will occur. The acceptable level of these variations differs for each system and each application. A problem exists when these variations drift beyond acceptable limits or when the output signal is non-existent.

A fiber optic system has three sections. Each section may have many components and any number of these components may be the cause of the problem. The goal of troubleshooting a defective system is to isolate the fault to some area of the system before attempting to identify the flawed components.

Following a flowchart or a logical process will help isolate a problem. Each fiberoptic system is different and will have a unique troubleshooting process. This makes it important for you to be familiar with the system you are working on. with the systam you are working on.
